## The three selections

### 1b. Drell-Yan

<!-- hand:dy_notes -->
**JAM24's two collider Z records are NNPDF records.** JAM fits fitpack `zrap/1000` and
`wzhep` ATLAS7C_Wp / ATLAS7C_Wm / ATLAS7C_Z, and each is the same measurement as an NNPDF set,
**value for value** (checked 2026-09-10): `zrap/1000` is `CDFZRAP_NEW`, and the three `wzhep`
tables are the W+, W- and Z-peak rows of `ATLASWZRAP11CC`. `jam_data` selects the NNPDF copies of
the two Z tables, whose commondata carry the bin edges; the fitpack twins stay `reader_only` as
duplicates, so the union cannot count a row twice. The two W tables are blocked with every other
W record (section 2).

**No W record is fitted.** Ten W records (`w.cms8_*`, `w.lhcb7_*`, `w.lhcb8_*`, `w.atlas7_46fb_*`,
`w.atlas7_36pb_*`, 98 rows) are contracted with their rows, edges, charges and cuts, and stay
`reader_only`: PIXEL's single-lepton kernel `DYLeptonEtaKernel` has no `evolved_tensor`, so it
cannot compose the evolution this closure applies to every Drell-Yan row (measured 2026-09-10).

All of section 1b past E866 is **structurally validated only**: row counts, edges, cuts and
covariance against the commondata, not row-by-row against NNPDF's FK predictions.
<!-- /hand:dy_notes -->

**`dy.e866_pd_10002` is in none of the three.** fitpack dy/10001 is E866 *pp* absolute and
10002 is E866 *pd* absolute, while 20001/20002 are the pd-over-2pp ratios. JAM fits 10001 +
the ratios; NNPDF fits `DYE886P` (pp) + `DYE886R` (the ratio). Neither fits E866 pd
absolute. It stays `selectable: true` and can be added back explicitly.

## 2. Not included, and why

Classes, because "unavailable" was hiding situations that call for completely different work. `pixel.data.closure_datatypes` carries these per datatype with a **dated** blocker; a record's own blocker is its contract's `drop_reason`.

| class | meaning | what would change it |
|---|---|---|
| **scope** | implemented; excluded by an analysis decision | a decision, not development |
| **field** | no field in this fit for it to constrain | adding a sector (FFs, helicity, pion) |
| **cuts** | every row falls outside the closure's Q2/W2 cuts | a change of cuts |
| **duplicate** | the same measurement is fitted under another id | nothing -- counted once |
| **wiring** | builder **and** data both present here; nothing reads one into the other | a layout arm |
| **builder** | PIXEL has the operator; the closure has no arm for this observable | a closure arm |
| **data** | builder exists; numbers or edges are not in the local trees | fetch from HEPData |
| **physics** | the coefficient, matching or correction does not exist in PIXEL | research |

<!-- hand:not_included_intro -->
**Read `rawdata/` and `filter.py`, not `kinematics*.yaml`.** The processed kinematics store
bin **centres**; edges, beam energies, fiducial regions and lepton charges are in the
HEPData tables under `rawdata/`, and the row order is whatever `filter.py` writes. Two
classifications in this file were wrong until 2026-09-10 for exactly that reason.
<!-- /hand:not_included_intro -->

## 3. The short version

* **Fitted:** the union's 46 datasets / 4467 rows; JAM24 29 / 3005; NNPDF4.0 45 / 4433.
* **JAM24 `input.py`:** 16 of 213 entries fitted; the rest by class: field 156, scope 27, cuts 1, physics 13.
* **NNPDF4.0 roster:** 26 fitted whole, 4 in part (physics 4), 13 not (scope 7, builder 1, data 1, physics 4).
<!-- hand:short_version -->
* **Collider Drell-Yan is no longer blocked on wiring.** Every Z set either analysis fits is
  selected or blocked for a stated reason of another class. **No W record is fitted**: all ten
  are wired and wait on one PIXEL capability, evolution in `DYLeptonEtaKernel`.
* **The fitted collider data is structurally validated only.** None of it has been compared
  row-by-row against NNPDF's FK predictions (`pixel/plans/closure_missing_observables.md` §8).
* **Out by scope or field:** fragmentation functions, helicity PDFs, the pion PDF, JAM's own
  lattice inputs, and every ratio and asymmetry (PIXEL implements the ratio operators).
* **Blocked on PIXEL work: 6** -- NuTeV dimuon (x2), inclusive jets (NLO needs an IR
  subtraction), W+charm and leading neutron (no operator), the recoil correction
  `ATLASLOMASSDY11EXT` needs, and evolution in the lepton-level kernel for every W record.
* **Data to fetch: one set.** `CMSDY2D11`'s mass-bin edges, from HEPData `ins1262319`.
  `ATLAS_WZ_TOT_13TEV` also needs its total-vs-fiducial status read from arXiv 1603.09222;
  that is a transcription, not missing numbers.
<!-- /hand:short_version -->

## 4. What running the collider data takes

<!-- hand:run_costs -->
Measured 2026-09-10.

* **Speed.** PIXEL used to rebuild each binned node's NLO hard tensor for every (kernel,
  evolution) group -- 680 groups over 30 kernels on a Z table, about 43 minutes per row. It now
  builds it once per kernel per node, and since 2026-09-10 evaluates each basis row once per
  quadrature point instead of once per kernel: **0.22 s per node per hard kernel** (was 0.79 s),
  and one CDF row builds and folds in **22 s** with warm evolution caches. The 15 selected Z
  records (316 rows) come to an estimated **14 CPU-hours** per truth member (was ~50),
  `z.atlas8_lomass_2d` alone about 8, and the batched pass is single-process. The first run
  after any change to PIXEL's kernel source rebuilds the cached evolution operators (the cache
  is keyed on a hash of that source). Since 2026-09-10 those are built in batches -- every
  scale and channel of a record sharing one pass over each contour block -- and a cold CDF row
  builds and folds in 38 s, against 62 s one operator at a time. Records with many mass nodes
  batch up to 8 scales per pass; that saving has not been measured at full scale.
* **CHORUS kernels: ~16 h per beam, now roughly 40 min.** Since the closure moved to the
  146-node piecewise-quintic basis (2026-09-09), PIXEL's structure-function matching rebuilt
  4.6 GiB of Mellin moments for every (contribution, Q2) -- they no longer fit its 1 GiB memo --
  so a CHORUS beam (23 contributions x 260 distinct Q2) was an estimated 23 x 260 x 9.5 s.
  Fixed 2026-09-10 in `pixel/src/pixel/kernels/matching.py` (moments built once per kernel,
  coefficients folded into the rows). Measured after: ~14 s per kernel plus ~0.3 s per extra
  Q2, so a 260-Q2 kernel is ~1.5 min and a beam roughly 35-40 min on one core -- extrapolated
  from 3 of the 23 contributions, all non-singlet, measured beside other load. The closure's
  CHORUS test went from 1171 s to 295 s.
* **Memory.** A fit keeps one `(rows, 146, 146)` tensor per group: E605 alone is 13.8 GB, the
  Z records about 37 GB. The full-suite fits need the big machine, collider data or not.
* **The uncertainty floor was wrong for every Drell-Yan row until today.** The fold added an
  absolute 1e-6 to sigma, sized for order-one DIS values, while PIXEL's Drell-Yan predictions
  are around 1e-7 (E866) to 1e-16 (a Z row at the pole). Committed small-suite E866 data had
  sigma/|mean| of 2.2 against a published 0.15. The Drell-Yan floor is now relative to each
  record's scale, in all eight suites.
* **Normalization is not validated.** Relative errors make a closure insensitive to the
  prediction's absolute scale, and none of the binned predictions has been compared with
  NNPDF's FK tables (`pixel/plans/closure_missing_observables.md` §8).
<!-- /hand:run_costs -->
